answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines the following rules concerning sabbatical leaves (Article 5.20 - Sabbatical Leave):

1. A sabbatical leave is for a period of twelve (12) months, commencing on 1 July, or for six (6) months commencing on 1 January. No portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement. A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (page 5, 22.07).

2. Members who terminate their employment between June 1 and Labour Day, and who have no formal teaching duties during all or part of that period, shall take and be deemed to have taken as much of their vacation entitlement as possible during that period (page 5, Article 5.20).

3. In the event of the death of a Member, the value of any unused vacation entitlement will be paid to her/his estate (page 5, Article 5.20).

4. When Members take a sabbatical leave after three (3) years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement. If the sabbatical is postponed, the Member shall receive one (1) year sabbatical credit for the year postponed so that their next sabbatical leave will occur according to their original sabbatical rotation (page 5, Sabbaticals after three (3) years can be granted provided that Members have tenure when the leave is taken).

5. Immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer (page 6, 12.20).

Regarding benefits during sabbatical leaves:

- Members will be covered for periods of sick leave to the extent of the actual salary paid during that period as per Article 7.55 – Physical and Mental Illness (page 4, 7.55).
- Members must be provided with specific information concerning coverage for Long-Term Disability at the time of appointment. Members may contribute to the pension plan on the basis of their actual salary, and life insurance may be carried based on the Member's actual salary (page 4, no specific article number).
- The value of any unused vacation entitlement will be paid to the estate of a deceased Member (page 5, Article 5.20).

The employer's retirement plan is outlined in several sections of the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement.

1. Pension Plan: The Defined Benefit component of the Retirement Plan and Member contributions shall only be used towards funding the Defined Benefit component of the Retirement Plan (8.45.3). The Employer's cost of those benefit plans in which the Member does not retain participation will be added to the early retirement incentive (16b). Should the Member die during the Special Voluntary Early Retirement Period, the payment will cease at the end of the month the death occurred (17). A Member taking Special Voluntary Early Retirement would enjoy all retiree privileges as well as tuition fee waiver (18).

3. Academic Freedom: Academic staff have the right to exercise their civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded or hindered by the Employer (3.10.4). answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement (2008-11) states that a Member can take a sabbatical leave after three years, but all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided (page 135). Sabbaticals can be granted if the Member has tenure when the leave becomes effective, such a leave does not require the postponement of a sabbatical leave for a Member with six or more years of service, and the leave does not have a negative impact on the budget of the Department/School (page 135).

After the sabbatical leave, Members are required to return to the University to resume responsibilities as a full-time Member of faculty for at least six months. Failure to return may require the Member to reimburse the University for all salary and benefits received during the leave, unless the Member is planning to retire in the academic year immediately following the sabbatical leave or has agreed to an early sabbatical leave without financial penalty (page 136).

Members must also prepare and forward a full written account of their scholarly and professional activities and accomplishments within one month of their return (page 136).

Study leaves, which are leaves for the purpose of upgrading academic qualifications, can be granted to a tenured, probationary, or Permanent Sessional Member after two years of full-time service, but no sooner than two years after a sabbatical leave (Article 7.30). The maximum length of leaves to be granted during a Member's academic career shall normally not exceed two years (page 136).

A member who is on sabbatical shall report to the University all non-trivial income for professional services from sources other than the University, and such income together with the sabbatical salary continuation shall not exceed 100% of the faculty member’s normal University income plus reasonable research, travel, and associated expenses (Collective Agreement 2015-2018, page 33).

This is outlined in Article 7.25 – Sabbatical Leaves of the Collective Agreement 2008-11, 2011-14, and 2016-2020. The purpose of sabbatical leaves is to allow Members to engage in further training, advanced studies, scientific or creative work, improve the University's relations with other universities, gain practical or professional experience, or to spend part or all of their sabbatical leave on campus (Section 7.25.1 Preamble). The agreement states that when Members take a sabbatical leave, all accumulated years of eligibility entitlement are exhausted unless otherwise provided for in the Collective Agreement (Section 7.25.2 Eligibility). answer:
The academic personnel committee, as stated in the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 85), is responsible for reviewing the assessments by the Department/School and the Dean/University Librarian on applications for contract renewal, tenure, promotion, and merit increments. The committee helps to ensure that all applications have been fairly and completely assessed according to the terms of the Collective Agreement. The review results in either an endorsement or a refusal to endorse the assessments, which are communicated in writing to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost. The committee's advice is considered by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost in making a decision on the application.

In each faculty, there is a Faculty Personnel Committee composed of five elected Members plus two alternates. The committee's structure includes a non-voting Chair appointed by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost. There should be no more than two Members belonging to the same academic Department/School, and at least two Members should be Full Professors from within that Faculty (page 86).

There is also a Francophone Faculty Personnel Committee with similar responsibilities, composed of five elected Members plus two alternates. The Members of this committee must be qualified Francophone Members, either teaching faculty who have taught or are scheduled to teach a course in French at Laurentian, or librarian faculty who have provided or are scheduled to provide library service in French at Laurentian (page 86). Two of the six Members of the Francophone Faculty Personnel Committee must be Full Professors/Librarians, except as provided in clause 5.55.7. Potential candidates will be identified by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost (page 87).

However, cases involving the inability of a member to perform reasonable duties due to physical or emotional illness are treated separately from cases of dismissal for cause.

Regarding removal from office, the agreement does not specifically mention it. The collective agreement for the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) states that in cases of redundancy, a Redundancy Committee is formed to make recommendations. This committee, in consultation with the Vice-President, Academic and Provost, the Dean/University Librarian, and the Faculty/Library Personnel Committee, is responsible for recommending which full-time members of the Bargaining Unit will be affected by redundancy (Clauses 11.10.8 and 10.10.8).

If the Redundancy Committee decides that members with tenure or on a three-year probationary contract will be affected by redundancy, it shall include in its final recommendation to the Employer a list of administrative and academic areas to which the members could be transferred, with or without a year's retraining, considering their academic and professional qualifications (Clauses 11.10.10 and 10.10.10).

If the Employer approves a resolution to act on the Redundancy Committee's recommendation that a member be declared redundant, the Employer shall send the member a written notice of its resolution. This notice shall also contain an offer to the tenured member of several options, including voluntary early retirement, transfer to another Department/School, transfer to an appropriate administrative vacancy in the University, termination of employment with severance pay, or any other alternative with the mutual consent of the two Parties (Clauses 11.10.11 and 10.10.11).

However, the University and the Members shall share equally in the "net proceeds" derived therefrom. The name of the University shall not be used in connection with inventions in which the Employer has no interest without mutual agreement (page 65, 6.30.9). Any revenue that the Employer may receive from inventions shall be dedicated to academic development and research, with at least 50% of such income designated for academic development and research in the Faculty/Library with which the inventor is affiliated (page 65, 6.30.10). The Employer shall not enter any agreement to sub-contract work or responsibilities already undertaken or possessed by the Employer and the Members without securing to the Members all the rights, privileges, and benefits accorded to them in this patent Article of this Collective Agreement (page 65, 6.30.11).

In terms of copyright, the Member who is the creator of any work shall retain the copyright therein unless otherwise stated in this Article (page 65, 6.35.1). The University shall hold copyright to any work produced by Members as part of their normal workload for the University for use in its distance education courses (page 65, 6.35.2). Members shall receive, upon request, a copy of any work produced by them for the University and to which the University holds copyright under the terms of this Collective Agreement, provided the cost does not exceed the cost of the tape/film/recording or other medium upon which the work has been produced (page 67, 6.35.16 and 6.35.17).

Disputes arising out of Articles 6.30 – Patents and 6.35 – Copyright shall be handled following a specific grievance and arbitration procedure (pages 66-67, 6.40.1-6.40.3). A continuing Committee on Patents and Copyright is established to mediate these disputes and make recommendations for their resolution (page 66, 6.40.2). This Committee shall meet at least twice annually to conduct such business as is referred to it, consider strategies for marketing inventions, improvements, or discoveries, and recommend modifications or changes in the patents and copyright Articles of this Collective Agreement (page 66, 6.40.2a-c).

answer: The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides that disciplinary action shall be just and reasonable, commensurate with the offense. Cause for disciplinary measures includes serious unprofessional behavior and failure to comply with the provisions of the agreement (excluding minor technical violations). answer: Removal from office due to illness or disability is handled differently than dismissal for just cause in the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement. If a member is unable to perform reasonable duties due to physical or mental illness, leave shall be granted, and the case shall be dealt with within the University's sickness and disability provisions (Article 2.41, page 47 for 2002-2005; Article 7.55, page 101 for 2011-14). If the member refuses to comply with the requirements of these provisions, the President may proceed to lay dismissal charges (Article 2.41, page 48 for 2002-2005; Article 7.55, page 101 for 2011-14). However, it's a sufficient defence to prevent dismissal if the member can establish that failure to perform reasonable duties arose from physical or mental illness (Article 2.41, page 48 for 2002-2005; Article 7.55, page 101 for 2011-14). The member shall present medical evidence to their Dean/Director of the Library if they believe they have recovered and are capable of undertaking normal academic activities (Article 2.41, page 48 for 2002-2005; Article 7.55, page 101 for 2011-14).

The collective agreement for Laurentian University Faculty Association provides regulations for members' academic workload as follows:

1. Teaching Members:
   - The maximum normal teaching load per academic year is two (2) full courses or twelve (12) credit equivalents in the Faculty of Science and Engineering, and two and one-half (2 ½) full courses or fifteen (15) credit equivalents in other Faculties (Collective Agreement 2008-11, page 70).

2. Professional Librarian and Archivist Members:
   - The normal hours of scheduled student contact shall not exceed twelve (12) per week, scheduled fairly and equitably, on the recommendation of the Department (Collective Agreement 2008-11, page 70).

3. Annual Academic Workload:
   - The President must ensure that the annual academic workload is determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible, taking into account various factors, such as member's program needs, course preparation, grading, and administration, academic counseling and consulting, student enrollments, and the method of course delivery (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 20).
   - Full-time faculty shall have a normal teaching load of 15 credits per academic year, which includes a minimum of 12 credits taught live, subject to certain exceptions (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 21).

answer:
The rules concerning annual reports for members, as outlined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement 2016-2020, are as follows:

1. Full-time academic staff, including librarians, are required to submit an annual report by June 1 of each year, reviewing their Academic Activity for the period May 1-April 31 (LUFA-H, 17). In the case of Sabbatical/Study Leave, this report should generally be submitted within one month upon return from leave. The annual report should consist of:
   - An updated curriculum vitae using the HU template
   - Copies of Senate-approved standardized student evaluations
   - A completed report based on the HU report template
   - Electronic copies of presentations
   - An update on doctoral studies (LUFA-H, 17)

2. Sessional Members are required to submit brief annual reports in electronic format to the Dean/University Librarian (LUFA-H, not specified page number). These reports should include a current curriculum vitae as well as a current teaching dossier as defined in Article 5.50 – Assessment of a Member’s Performance. At their discretion, Sessional Members may also include material related to their scholarly or creativity activity, professional development, university governance, outside professional activities, and service to the community (LUFA-H, not specified page number).

3. Full-time members of the Bargaining Unit shall submit a written Report on their activities for the preceding twelve months, from 1 May to 30 April, to the President by June 22nd. The report will cover all components of members’ activities as described in Article 10, Academic Activity. In preparing their Annual Report, members shall use the standardized form approved by the University of Sudbury Senate and provided by the Registrar, and it is also their responsibility to provide annually an up-to-date C.V. with their Annual Report (LUFA-H, not specified page number).

answer:
Faculty appointments at Laurentian University, according to the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020 (page 23), are made through a process that prioritizes Members with established courses. If an appointment cannot be filled by a Member with establishment, appointments will be made from rosters of potential instructors who have taught in the department in the previous academic year. If a suitable candidate cannot be found in the roster, the appointments will be advertised on employment websites (page 23).

The application process includes the submission of a curriculum vitae, a current teaching dossier, reference letters, and any relevant supplementary information (page 23). Three academic letters of reference speaking specifically to the position will be sent directly to the Employer for new applicants, new course offerings, or courses out of the applicant's expertise or department (page 23).

For adjunct faculty appointments, a list is tabled at Senate each month, including the names, Department/School affiliations, periods of appointment, a justification for each appointment, highest degree held, year obtained, current institution and rank (position), at that institution. Adjunct faculty Members may become Sessional Members if they carry duties consistent with the Collective Agreement, and they will be included in the faculty listing on Department/School websites (pages 7-8).

Cross appointments, which allow Members to be appointed to more than one Department/School of the University, can be made for academic teaching/scholarly or professional reasons, but only with the consent of all Departments/Schools concerned. Cross appointments are made by the Employer for a fixed period not exceeding five years and may be renewed or altered with the consent of the Member and on the recommendations of the Department(s)/School(s) concerned (pages 7-8).

Assessments for the renewal, promotion, and tenure of Members are based on an assessment of their performance in teaching, scholarly activity, and university, professional, and community service, as set out in Articles 10 and 11.04 of the Collective Agreement (page 11). The nature and scope of past teaching activities are taken into account in assessing a Member, and the assessors will look for evidence that the applicant has recognized problems in teaching, taken steps to improve, and made improvements that are reflected in independent evidence provided by the member (page 11). The assessors shall be flexible in assessing stronger performance in some areas against weaker performance in other areas, but they shall not recommend tenure for an applicant if teaching performance is judged unsatisfactory or if the applicant is not engaged in a program of scholarly activity (page 11).

answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides that academic freedom is essential for the teaching and research activities of the University (0.02 Academic freedom). Academic freedom includes the right to investigate, speculate, and comment publicly, to carry out research, to publish results, to choose and pursue teaching methods and content, to state professional views, to discuss and criticize, including respectful criticism of the Employer, the Union, and any public or private institution, and to be free from institutional censorship (3.10.2). The principle and practice of collegial governance are essential for the exercise of academic freedom within the University (3.10.3). Members have the right to exercise their civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded, or hindered by the Employer (3.10.4). The Employer shall not abridge academic freedom on any grounds, including claims of institutional autonomy (3.10.5). Members have the right to privacy, consistent with the traditions of academic freedom (3.10.6, 3.15.1).

answer:
Academic freedom, as defined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 2), includes several conditions:

1. The right to search for truth, knowledge, and understanding, and to express freely what one believes (3.10.2).
2. Freedom in teaching, research, and scholarship, including the right to disseminate and publish results (3.10.2).
3. Freedom to produce and perform creative works (3.10.2).
4. Freedom to acquire, preserve, and provide access to documentary material in all formats (3.10.2).
5. Freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies (3.10.2).
6. Freedom to engage in service to the institution and the community (3.10.2).
7. Freedom to express one’s opinion about the University, its administration, and the system in which one works (3.10.2).
8. Academic freedom does not confer legal immunity but requires the acknowledgement of the work of others and the acceptance of responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances (3.10.2).
9. The principle and practice of collegial governance are essential for the exercise of academic freedom within the University (3.10.3).
10. Academic freedom also entails the right of academic staff to exercise their civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded, or hindered by the Employer (3.10.4).
11. The Employer shall not abridge academic freedom on any grounds, including claims of institutional autonomy (3.10.5).
12. Members have a right to privacy, consistent with the traditions of Academic Freedom and the provisions of this Article (3.15.1).

In addition, the Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (page 3) further explains that academic freedom makes commitment possible, does not require neutrality in expression or attitude, and carries the responsibility to respect the right of other members of the academic community to express their opinions (0.02 Academic freedom, section b). Furthermore, academic freedom is not absolute but depends upon a collective commitment of Members to exercise that principle in a manner consistent with their scholarly obligations as professors to base research and teaching on an honest and responsible search for knowledge and to uphold the norms of civil discourse (0.02 Academic freedom, section d).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines the rights, responsibilities, and duties of the members of the bargaining unit. The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement addresses health, safety, and security through Article 3.25 - Health, Safety, and Security. According to the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 22), the Employer recognizes a responsibility to provide an environment intended to protect the health, safety, and security of employees as they carry out their responsibilities. answer: The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides that discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.1). Just cause for disciplinary measures includes serious unprofessional behavior and failure to comply with any provisions of the collective agreement, minor technical violations excepted (5.75.2). The forms of discipline that may be taken against a full-time member include a letter of reprimand, suspension with pay, suspension without pay, withholding of an annual increment, and dismissal (5.75.3). For a sessional or part-time member, the forms of discipline include a letter of reprimand, suspension with pay, suspension without pay, removal of seniority and/or establishment, and dismissal (5.75.5). Discipline shall be imposed only in compliance with principles of natural justice and due process, and the member has a fundamental right to know the nature of the allegations against them and to respond to such allegations (5.75.4). The collective agreement also specifies that cases involving the inability of a member to perform reasonable duties due to physical or mental illness shall be treated separately from cases for disciplinary measures (5.75.6). Grievances regarding disciplinary measures against sessional members shall be dealt with by the procedures in clause 4.40.7 of Article 4.40 (5.75.7). Dismissal means the termination for just cause of a term appointment or a probationary appointment before the end of the stated contractual period, or the termination of a tenure appointment for just cause at any time other than normal retirement (5.80.1).

answer:
Removal from office, in the context of the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, is referred to as "Dismissal" (Article 4.65 - Dismissal Procedures). According to the agreement, dismissal means the termination for just cause of a term appointment or a probationary appointment before the end of the stated contractual period, or the termination of a tenure appointment for cause at any time other than normal retirement (4.65.1). Just cause for dismissal is defined as gross misconduct or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibilities as defined in the agreement either through incompetence or neglect of duties (4.65.2).

However, cases involving the inability of a member to perform reasonable duties by reason of physical or emotional illness shall be treated separately from cases of dismissal for cause (4.65.3). If such inability has been established, leave shall be granted, and the case dealt with within the University sickness and disability provisions (4.65.3a). If the member refuses to comply with the requirements of the University's sickness and disability provisions, the President may proceed with dismissal for cause. But it shall be a sufficient defense to prevent dismissal for the member to establish that failure to perform reasonable duties arose from physical or emotional illness (4.65.3c).

If members are on sickness or disability leave and consider that they have recovered and are capable of undertaking normal academic activities, they shall present medical evidence from a medical practitioner to the President (4.65.3d).

The source document for the information is the 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, page 35.

When the Employer becomes aware of a matter that may lead to the imposition of discipline, including investigations triggered by a formal complaint pursuant to a discrimination and harassment policy, the Employer shall commence an investigation within twenty working days (5.75.6). The member and the Union shall be notified in writing of the nature of the allegation(s) upon commencement of the investigation (5.75.6).

answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement, Full-time academic staff have the right and responsibility to devote a reasonable proportion of their time to scholarly activity. This activity includes (but is not limited to) research directed towards a contribution to knowledge, the dissemination of its results, participation in academic activities that contribute to the enhancement, creation, and dissemination of knowledge, and creative and professional activities which contribute to one's discipline (11.03, 5.15.20-22).

Scholarly activity may involve activities such as the writing and publication of books, articles, case studies, the development of teaching materials, research for a doctoral dissertation, the writing of book reviews, presentations at conferences, and demonstrated leadership in professional education (11.03, 5.15.22). However, it's important to note that these activities must be of good quality and consistent with the contribution to knowledge described in the agreement (11.03, 5.15.20, 5.15.22).

Members are also encouraged to deposit one signed copy of their published material in the Huntington University Library and a hard or electronic copy in the Office of the President (11.03, 5.15.25). They have the right to participate in the activities of professional or learned societies, providing such activities do not conflict with the reasonable fulfillment of assigned duties (11.03, 5.15.26).

For the purposes of the Collective Agreement, scholarly activity does not normally include research directly related to the immediate and normal preparation for teaching activity (5.15.23). The Parties also agree that Members shall indicate affiliation with the University and acknowledge their indebtedness to students and their academic colleagues in relation to their own research (5.15.24).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement provides that during leaves under Article 25, members can continue to participate in pension and benefit plans, and their applicable shares of contributions and/or premiums will be paid unless they elect not to do so in writing. Additionally, the term "another Member of an Employee’s family" is defined in the collective agreement to include specific relatives such as grandparents, guardians, grandchildren, daughters-in-law, and sons-in-law. (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 7)

Les activités universitaires sont définies à l'article 10 de la Convention collective 2015-2018. Les membres de l'unité de négociation s'engagent à effectuer les tâches d'enseignement, de recherche, à fournir leurs services à l'Université et à la profession et à la communauté. Les conditions applicables à ces activités universitaires sont que :

- Les activités doivent être effectuées dans des proportions raisonnables, variant selon les personnes.
- Les membres ont jusqu'au 31 août pour répondre par écrit aux réserves du Recteur concernant leur rendement en matière d'activités universitaires.
- Si la réponse écrite du membre ne répond pas de manière satisfaisante aux réserves du Recteur, le cas est confié au Comité des affaires professorales. Les motifs à l'appui sont fournis par écrit.
- Le Comité des affaires professorales évalue les activités du membre, les réserves écrites du Recteur et, le cas échéant, la réponse du membre. Le comité fait au Recteur une recommandation sur la question de savoir si les activités sont satisfaisantes ou non, en précisant par écrit les raisons de sa recommandation et, le cas échéant, la réponse du membre.
- La recommandation du comité est faite au plus tard 28 jours civils après que le cas lui a été soumis par le Recteur.
- Le Recteur évalue et prend en compte la recommandation du Comité des affaires professorales et rend sa décision finale en se reportant aux points pertinents de l'article 10. Lorsqu'il s'agit d'accepter une recommandation positive, l'augmentation est accordée rétroactivement au 1er juillet.

answer: La Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne (2017-2020) prévoit un soutien à la recherche annuel de 160 000 $ (article 6.25-1), qui est fourni par l'Employeur au vice-recteur à la recherche pour encourager la productivité en travaux d'érudition. Tout membre du corps professoral peut participer à ce concours ouvert (article 6.25-1). answer:
Selon l'article 6.35 et l'article 15 de la Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne, voici les informations clés sur les droits d'auteur :

**Droits d'auteur revenant aux Membres :**

* Le membre conserve les droits d'auteur pour toute création intellectuelle sauf stipulation contraire (art. 6.35.1).
* Les créations couvertes par cette disposition comprennent notamment des œuvres imprimées, des programmes informatiques, du matériel pédagogique en ligne, des tableaux, des sculptures, des films, des diapositives et d'autres (art. 6.35.1).

**Droits d'auteur revenant à l'Université :**

* Les parties conviennent que l'Université détient les droits d'auteur pour toute création intellectuelle produite par un membre dans le cadre de ses fonctions à l'Université (art. 6.35.2).
* L'Université conserve également les droits d'auteur pour toutes les œuvres originales, y compris des livres, textes, articles, monographies, glossaires, bibliographies, matériel cartographique, affiches, manuels d'étude, plans de cours, examens, directives de travaux et autres supports visuels (art. 15.01).

**Copie du membre :**

* Si possible après en avoir fait la demande, le membre doit recevoir une copie de toute propriété intellectuelle qu'il a produite pour l'Université, sans que le coût excède celui du moyen utilisé (art. 6.35.16).
* Cela signifie que les membres ont droit à une copie des œuvres pour lesquelles l'Université détient les droits d'auteur, moyennant un coût limité.

**Effacement ou destruction de l'œuvre :**

* En cas de désir de l'Université d'effacer ou de détruire en tout ou en partie un ouvrage pour lequel elle détient les droits d'auteur, le membre doit être notifié et a droit à une copie de l'œuvre (art. 6.35.17).

La Convention collective garantit ainsi que les membres conservent les droits d'auteur sur leurs créations sauf stipulation contraire, tandis que l'Université détient les droits d'auteur pour toutes les œuvres produites par les membres dans le cadre de leurs fonctions.

Selon la Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne, les augmentations annuelles à titre de progression dans le rang sont définies comme suit :

* Les augmentations sont accordées aux membres à temps plein sur la base d'une évaluation annuelle des tâches accomplies (20.01).

* Lorsque les tâches accomplies sont jugées satisfaisantes, l'augmentation est accordée (20.03).

De plus, la Convention précise que lorsqu'un membre est promu à un rang supérieur dans une année donnée, l'augmentation à titre de progression dans le rang pour cette même année est celle du rang supérieur (20.07).

Selon l'article 8 de la Convention Collective 2018-2021, un Comité des affaires professorales est créé pour faire des recommandations justifiées au Recteur à la suite des demandes faites par les membres en matière de renouvellement de nominations à l'essai, promotion, permanence, subventions de recherche ou de voyages et congés sabbatiques (page 10).

Le Comité est composé de :

* Un représentant ayant la permanence élu par le Département parmi les membres permanents (article 8.02.a, page 10)
* Deux Membres non désignés, ayant la permanence ou à l’essai élus (article 8.02.b, page 10)
* Un membre non désigné à plein temps pour agir comme substitut (article 8.02.c, page 10)
* Le Doyen de la Faculté des arts de l'Université Laurentienne, sans droit de vote (article 8.02.d, page 10)

En outre, si le Recteur a des réserves à propos du rendement d'un membre concernant les activités universitaires décrites à l'article 10, il envoie un exposé de ses réserves au membre au plus tard le 31 juillet (article 20.04.a, page 41). Le membre a jusqu'au 31 août pour y répondre par écrit (article 20.04.b, page 41). Si la réponse écrite du membre ne répond pas de manière satisfaisante aux réserves du Recteur, le cas est confié au Comité des affaires professorales et les motifs à l'appui sont communiqués au membre (article 20.04.c, page 41).

Source : Convention collective 2018-2021, pages 10, 41 et 59.

- Il assure, dans la mesure du possible, que les membres de l'unité ont l'occasion de participer à la prise de décisions, à l'élaboration de politiques et aux tâches administratives de l'unité.

Ces conditions ne sont pas spécifiquement liées à une discipline spécifique ou à une année spécifique. Cependant, les proportions dans lesquelles les membres se consacrent à ces activités peuvent varier selon les personnes.

answer: La convention définit maladie physique et mentale comme une incapacité due à un accident ou à une maladie, qui peut valider un congé de maladie de durée maximale de six mois. Les activités universitaires s'appliquent aux membres de l'unité de négociation qui, en tant qu'universitaires, se consacrent à la transmission et à l'expression créatrice du savoir, à son éclaircissement et à l'élargissement de ses frontières, à l'administration universitaire et au service à la profession et à la communauté (Article 10.01, page 37). Certaines des activités mentionnées dans le contexte sont la rédaction ou la direction et la publication de livres, manuels pédagogiques, revues spécialisées et articles (page 37), la participation à des colloques à titre de conférencier ou d'auditeur (page 37), la production d'images, notamment des photographies et des œuvres architecturales (page 37), les recherches menées à l'aide de connaissances traditionnelles/autochtones ainsi que l'application pratique ou la dissémination de telles recherches (page 37), et la bourse d'études autochtone (page 37).

answer:
La Convention collective prévoit que le processus de grief se déroule en deux étapes :

1. Étape 1 - Procédure informelle de grief : le Syndicat et l'Employeur conviennent de faire tous les efforts raisonnables pour régler informellement les griefs de façon expéditive et à l'amiable. Il est convenu qu'aucun grief ne peut être déposé avant que l'administrateur concerné ait eu l'occasion de corriger la situation dont se plaint le Syndicat. Cette plainte est discutée avec le membre de l'administration dans les 30 jours ouvrables suivant le moment où les circonstances donnant lieu à la plainte sont venues ou auraient dû raisonnablement venir à l'attention du Syndicat. L'administrateur donnera une réponse écrite dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la discussion. Si la plainte n’est pas réglée, elle sera acheminée au Recteur dans une 2° étape dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réponse.

2. Étape 2 - Procédure de grief par écrit : dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réponse mentionnée à la 1ère étape de la procédure, le Syndicat soumet par écrit au Recteur de l'Université un grief, en précisant la nature du grief, les dispositions particulières de la Convention collective qui sont présumées violées et la solution recherchée. Dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant le dépôt du grief, une réunion des représentants de l'Employeur avec le Syndicat et les membres concernés a lieu, à sa ou leur demande. Les Parties font des efforts raisonnables pour régler le grief et la réponse de l'Employeur est donnée dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réunion (source document : Convention collective 2017-2020, pages 25-26).

translated_question: What does the collective agreement have to say about pregnancy?
untranslated_answer:
According to Article 14.04 of the collective agreement (page not specified), there are provisions regarding maternity leave and benefits for Laurentian University Faculty Association members.

Here are some key points:

* The Employer provides a top-up to Employment Insurance maternity benefits, up to 100% of the employee's nominal salary during the pregnancy leave (Source: Article 14.04(a)).
* A maximum of 17 weeks of maternity leave will be granted in accordance with the Ontario Employment Standards Act (Source: Article 14.04(a)).
* To be eligible for additional Employment Insurance benefits, a member must have completed at least 12 months of active service without interruption (Source: Article 14.04(b)(i)).

1. **Recht auf Vorteile**: Fakultätsmitglieder mit freiwilliger reduzierter Arbeitszeit haben das Recht auf Vorteile, einschließlich Krankengeld, Langzeitinvaliditätspension, Beiträge zur Pensionsanlage, Lebensversicherung und Sabbatical-Urlaub (Artikel 7.35.3).
2. **Recht zum Beitrag zu den Vorteilen**: Mitglieder mit freiwilliger reduzierter Arbeitszeit können auf der Grundlage ihrer normalen vollen Vergütung Beiträge zu den Vorteilen leisten, wobei der Arbeitnehmer und der Arbeitgeber entsprechende Beiträge gemäß dem Kollektivvertrag erbringen (Artikel 7.35.3(c)).
3. **Recht auf Krankengeld**: Mitglieder haben Anspruch auf Krankengeld bis zu einer Höhe von sechs Monaten ansonsten vom Datum der Invalidität aus Anlass von Unfall oder Krankheit, für jede separate Invaliditätsursache (Artikel 7.55.1).
4. **Recht auf Langzeitinvaliditätspension**: Mitglieder, die eine freiwillige reduzierte Arbeitszeit planen, müssen spezifische Informationen über die Deckung während und nach der Zeit der freiwilligen reduzierten Arbeitszeit für Langzeitinvalidität erhalten (Artikel 7.35.3(b)).
5. **Recht auf Beförderungs- und Tenure-Politik**: Perioden von reduzierter Arbeitszeit sollen entsprechend der Reduzierung der Arbeitsbelastung im Rahmen von Tenure- und Beförderungs politik berücksichtigt werden (Artikel 7.35.5).
6. **Recht auf Vorteile während Urlaub ohne Entgelt**: Während eines Urlaubs ohne Entgelt sind Mitglieder berechtigt, keinen Lohn zu erhalten, dürfen aber an keinerlei Rechte oder Privilegien gemäß diesem Kollektivvertrag teilnehmen, außer wenn es um Vorteile unter Artikel 7.40 geht – Befreiung vom Urlaub ohne Entgelt (Artikel 7.40(b)).

Diese Punkte betonen die Bedeutung des Verständnisses der Rechte der Mitglieder wie im Kollektivvertrag ausgeführt.
translated_question: What does the agreement say about rights?

The Collective Agreement mentions several aspects related to "rights" of members. Here are some key points:

1. **Right to benefits**: Faculty Members on Voluntary Reduced Workload have the right to benefits, including sick leave, Long-Term Disability, Pension Plan contributions, Life Insurance, and Sabbatical Leave (Article 7.35.3).
2. **Right to contribute to the benefits plan**: Members on voluntary reduced workload may contribute to the benefits plan based on their normal full salary with appropriate contributions from the Employee and Employer as outlined in the Collective Agreement (Article 7.35.3(c)).
3. **Right to sick leave**: Members are eligible for sick leave up to a maximum of six months at salary otherwise receivable from the date of disability due to accident or illness, for each separate disability cause (Article 7.55.1).
4. **Right to Long-Term Disability benefits**: Members who plan to take a voluntary reduced workload must be provided with specific information concerning coverage for Long-Term Disability during and after the period of voluntary reduced workload (Article 7.35.3(b)).
5. **Right to tenure and promotion policies**: Periods of reduced workload shall be pro-rated in accordance with the reduction in workload for the application of tenure and promotion policies (Article 7.35.5).
6. **Right to benefits during leave without pay**: During a leave without pay, Members are entitled to leave without remuneration but may not participate in any rights or privileges under this Collective Agreement except regarding benefits governed by Article 7.40 – Leaves of Absence Without Pay (Article 7.40(b)).

These points highlight the importance of understanding the rights of members as outlined in the Collective Agreement.

* 40% scholarly activity, including commitments to external granting agencies
* 20% University governance, administrative duties, and other contributions to the University (Article 5.40.2).

untranslated_answer:
According to the collective agreement, there are specific rules regarding appointments and extensions.

For individuals with a limited-term contract (Article 5.20.14), they cannot make a promotion request during their last year of limited-term appointment unless they were prevented from doing so the previous year.

If the limited-term contract is renewed or if an individual receives a probationary (essai) appointment leading to permanence, they will be appointed anew at the rank they held during their previous appointment.

answer:
According to Article 7.20 - Absence - General in the Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page numbers not provided), the following are the rules concerning absence:

1. The University requires its Members to be available on a regular and ongoing basis to ensure that activities can be carried out in an orderly manner (7.20.1).
2. Any absence should not normally interfere with assigned or scheduled activities and the harmonious functioning of the Department/School (7.20.2).
3. Any absence from campus affecting teaching or professional librarian duties is governed by Article 5.15 - Rights, Responsibilities and Duties of Academics (7.20.3).
4. From Labour Day to Spring Convocation, absences of more than one week require notification to the Chair/Director and permission of the Dean/University Librarian. Shorter absences require notification to the Chair/Director (7.20.4).
5. From Spring Convocation to Labour Day, Departments/Schools must maintain a fair and equitable system to ensure a reasonable presence. Absences during this period must be in accordance with this system. Prior written permission is required for any absence of more than one week from the Dean/University Librarian (7.20.5).
6. Except where Members are on vacation, leave or other approved absence, they must remain in communication with their Department/School so that it is reasonably possible for the University to contact and/or recall them on short notice (7.20.6).
7. In exceptional cases, the University may recall a Member who is on vacation, leave, or formally approved absence. The University will not do so arbitrarily or unreasonably and will bear reasonable transportation costs consequent upon any such recall (7.20.7).

These rules outline the requirements for Members to be available and the procedures for taking absences, particularly during specific periods of the academic year.

According to Article 7.60 of the Collective Agreement (pages not specified), the collective agreement provides the following regarding pregnancy, parental and adoption leaves:

* Pregnancy leave:
	+ A pregnant full-time Member or pregnant Master Lecturer Member shall be entitled to seventeen (17) weeks pregnancy leave (7.60.1(a)).
	+ During the period of pregnancy leave, the Member shall receive from the Employer: 
		- For the first week, one-hundred percent (100%) of her nominal salary (7.60.1(b)(i));
		- For up to a maximum of sixteen (16) additional weeks, an amount equal to the difference between the Employment Insurance (EI) benefits received by the Member and one-hundred percent (100%) of the Member's nominal salary (7.60.1(b)(ii)).
* Parental leave on the occasion of the birth of a child:
	+ A Member who is a parent and who has opted to take parental leave under the Employment Insurance Act and applicable legislation shall be entitled to a parental leave of up to thirty-five (35) weeks (7.60.5(a)).
	+ During the period of parental leave, a Member shall receive from the Employer: 
		- For the first two (2) weeks, one-hundred percent (100%) of her/his nominal salary (7.60.5(b)(i));
		- For up to a maximum of seven (7) additional weeks, an amount equal to the difference between the EI benefits received by the Member and one-hundred percent (100%) of the Member's nominal salary (7.60.5(b)(ii)).
* Parental leave on the occasion of the adoption of a child:
	+ A Member who is a parent shall be entitled to a parental leave of up to thirty-seven (37) weeks (7.60.6(a)).
* Leave for parent not taking pregnancy or parental leave:
	+ On the occasion of the birth of a child or the adoption of a child coming into the care or custody of a parent for the first time, the child's parent who is not taking the pregnancy or parental leave shall be entitled to a leave with full salary and benefits of up to five (5) working days (7.60.4).
* Hospitalization:
	+ In the case where the newborn child is hospitalized, a Member may postpone or interrupt her pregnancy leave by the number of weeks the newborn child is hospitalized but it must be taken within the fifty-two (52) weeks from the date of the birth of the child (no specific article cited, but mentioned in multiple sections).

Note: The collective agreement mentions two versions, 2011-14 and 2017-2020. I assumed that the information provided applies to both versions unless otherwise specified.

answer:
The rules concerning resignation are as follows:

1. For Academic Staff, a Member may resign effective June 30 or December 30, with at least three (3) month's written notice to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost. All leaves to which a resigning Member would be entitled must be terminated at that date. (Article 5.85.1)

2. Employment may be terminated at any time by mutual written agreement between a Member and the Vice-President, Academic and Provost. (Article 5.85.2)

3. For Faculty Members on a leave of absence at another university, they are deemed to have resigned six (6) months after they receive tenure at that institution. (Article 5.85.3)

4. Professional Staff will provide their supervisor with a minimum of two (2) week’s notice prior to resigning from their position. (Article 5.85.4)

For retirement, the normal retirement date is the first (1st) day of July next following the attainment of age sixty-five (65), unless the Member's sixtieth birthday falls on the first (1st) day of July, in which case the Normal Retirement Date shall coincide with the Member's sixtieth birthday. Early retirement is governed by the regulations of the Laurentian University Pension Plan and Members retired from this University retain certain rights such as library privileges, parking privileges, University facilities, exemption from tuition fees for themselves, and the possibility to be bestowed the title of Professor/Librarian Emeritus upon retirement. (Article 5.90)

answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines the rights, responsibilities, and duties of academics in various areas. Here are some key points from the context provided:

1. Teaching/Professional Librarianship/Archives Management (Article 2.00): Members have the right to engage in these activities and are expected to participate actively. For members of the regular stream, this is a mandatory responsibility, while for alternate-stream members, it is expected but not always necessary in any given year.

2. Scholarly Activity (Article 2.00): Members have the right to engage in scholarly activities, which are inherent in their status as academics and flow naturally from their positions.

3. University Governance and Administrative Duties (Article 2.00): Members have the right to participate in university governance and administrative duties, and each member is entitled and expected to share in a reasonable amount of these responsibilities.

4. Outside Professional Activities, Service to the Community, Other Paid Activity (Article 2.00): These activities are undertaken voluntarily by the Member.

5. Bilingualism (Article 5.10): The Employer may require bilingualism for certain positions and consider it a desired qualification for specific responsibilities. A Member's performance in both French and English will be taken into consideration in matters such as promotion and tenure.

6. Rights, Responsibilities, and Duties of Academics (Article 5.15): Members have rights, duties, and responsibilities which derive from their positions as teachers/professional librarians and scholars working within the University community. They are expected to participate actively in Teaching/Professional Librarianship/Archives Management, Scholarly Activity, and University Governance and Administrative Duties, although not necessarily in all three in any one given year.

The Employer will reimburse claims at the rate of 100% to a maximum of $3,000, with official receipts or reasonable facsimiles as proof (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45).

Prior to sending the committee report to the President, the report must be brought to APC for review and approval. Members of the committee who wish to add a minority opinion may do so by submitting a written signed opinion which will be attached to the majority recommendation. Copies of the official ballots shall be made by the Chairperson, prior to sending the official ballots to the President. The Chairperson shall send the official ballots to the President, who shall retain them until all procedures up to and including arbitration have been exhausted and shall not be used for any other purpose (4.25.3).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines several rules concerning copyright in Articles 6.35 and 15. According to these articles:

* Except where the employer commissions or produces materials for assessment, grading, report, or correspondence as part of a member's normal duties (Article 15.02), the copyright for all forms of written, artistic, and recorded works is retained by the member responsible for origination.
* If the university requests a work under special contract, they are considered the first owner of the copyright (Article 6.35.3).
* Special contracts for distance education courses must allow contributors to use materials for their own classroom purposes, but not in another distance education course without written permission (Article 6.35.4).
* The university is responsible for the custody and control of works whose copyright they hold, including master copies (Article 6.35.5).
* Contributors must notify the university if they need to use incorporated materials, and the university has the right to refuse requests that are judged too expensive (Article 6.35.6).

The agreement also outlines a process for revisions, where authors can request changes after three years of use, and both parties will negotiate costs including the author's fee (Articles 6.35.9-11).

It's worth noting that Article 15.01 provides a broader definition of what constitutes copyrighted works, which may be relevant in certain situations.

The evaluation of applications shall be based upon an assessment of the member's performance in teaching, scholarly activity, and university, professional and community service as set out in Article 10, Academic Activity, and in addition for promotion, Article 11.04, Rank Criteria (page 12). Here are some key points from this section of the Collective Agreement:

1. Full-time members shall be entitled to a minimum of three weeks paid vacation per academic year, pro-rated for partial years (Article 7.02).

answer:
According to the Collective Agreement, dismissal procedures are outlined in various articles. 

For term and probationary appointments (Article 4.65), "dismissal" means termination for just cause before the end of the stated contractual period or normal retirement. Just cause includes gross misconduct and persistent failure to discharge academic responsibilities (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article 22.03).

However, cases involving inability to perform reasonable duties due to physical or emotional illness are treated separately from dismissal for cause (Collective Agreement 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA, Article 35; Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article 22.03). If a member refuses to comply with the requirements of the University's sickness and disability provisions or policies of the company carrying the insurance, the President may proceed with dismissal (Collective Agreement 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA, Article 35; Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article 22.03).

Furthermore, according to Article 22.04 of the Collective Agreement 2018-2021, when considering the possibility of dismissal, an investigation shall be completed in accordance with paragraphs (c) to (f) of Article 22.02.

Finally, under Article 4.65.4 of the Collective Agreement 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA, the President may suspend a member from some or all of their University duties and withdraw some or all of their University privileges for stated cause, excluding situations related to physical or emotional incapacity to perform reasonable duties.

Members on sabbatical leave are not normally assigned any formal workload or expected to participate in any formal University activities, except those required by the agreement. The compensation for sabbatical leaves coincides with the Collective Agreement in place, and salary, benefits, and other provisions will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association (Clause 22.09 of Collective Agreement 2018-2021). 30.01 Each full-time Member shall be eligible to receive a professional allowance for each

answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides guidelines for professional development of its members, specifically in relation to academic qualifications and performance assessment. These guidelines can be found in Articles 5.10 (Academic Qualifications Guidelines), 5.15 (Rights, Responsibilities and Duties of Academics), and 5.50 (Assessment of a Member's Performance).

1. Academic Qualifications: The qualifications for appointment or promotion to different ranks are specified in Article 5.10.2. For example, for the rank of Lecturer, a Master's degree or equivalent is required. For Assistant Professor, a Doctoral degree is necessary, along with satisfactory performance and evidence of scholarly activity over a five-year period. For Associate Professor, a Doctoral degree is required, along with teaching quality evaluation, evidence of scholarly activity, and at least five years of full-time teaching or relevant professional experience. 2. Teaching Evaluations: Members are expected to maintain their teaching dossiers annually, containing course syllabus, student evaluations, and other relevant material. The Vice-President, Academic and Provost communicates the decision on the request prior to the planned date of the course evaluation. (Source: Page 47)

3. Assessment Procedures: The applicant submits their academic dossier to the Dean/University Librarian by July 2, who makes it available to the Department/School by September 1. Members of the Department/School can access the applicant's dossier, and the applicant has the right to update it until the assessment is made. (Source: Page 48)

These guidelines aim to promote professional development and ensure fair evaluation of members' performance in academia. However, specific rules may vary depending on the rank and department of the faculty member.

The Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement outlines the conditions for sabbatical leave. To be eligible, a member must have been a full-time faculty member of the university for the past six consecutive years, holding the rank of Full Professor/Librarian, Associate Professor/Librarian, and Assistant Professor/Librarian at the time of application. They must also be tenured at the time their sabbatical leave begins.

During sabbatical leave, members who elect to remain on campus are entitled to suitable office space. If they are required to move their offices, moving and storage expenses will be paid by the employer. The employer may replace members on sabbatical leave when deemed necessary and has the right to limit the number of leaves granted in keeping with its academic responsibilities.

Sabbatical leave is not automatic and shall be granted following an approved application procedure. Time spent on sabbatical leave, study leave, or leave without pay does not count towards sabbatical eligibility. In exceptional circumstances and to attract qualified faculty, the Vice-President, Academic may grant credit towards a sabbatical leave for full-time faculty service at another university.

The agreement also states that under special circumstances, members may apply for sabbatical leave one year prior to the year in which they would normally become eligible. If granted, they will receive a stipend of 80% of their salary. The dean/university librarian may request that members apply for their sabbatical leave after the completion of five years (Sources: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 2008-11, 2011-14).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement defines Family Responsibility Leave for full-time faculty as follows:

answer:
Sabbatical leaves are addressed in Articles 12 of the Collective Agreement. The purpose of sabbatical leave is stated as "to foster the pursuit of knowledge and serve the academic and scholarly objectives of the University" (Article 12.01, page 34).

Eligibility for sabbatical leave varies depending on the type of leave being requested. Tenured members are eligible for a full year's leave after six years of employment since their last sabbatical or a half-year's leave after three years (Article 12.02, page 34). Limited-term appointees who are subsequently hired into a tenure-track position within three years may have all their previous service counted towards eligibility (Article 12.03, page 35).

The process for applying for sabbatical leave involves providing a dossier to the Chair by September 30 of the year prior to the leave, which includes plans and justification for the leave, as well as an updated CV (Article 12.05, page 36). The department must recommend approval or denial of the application by October 15, and the Faculty Affairs Committee will review the application and provide a recommendation to the President by December 15 (Articles 12.06-08, pages 37-38).

Additionally, the collective agreement outlines the responsibilities and expectations for members on sabbatical leave, including not being assigned formal workload or participating in formal activities, except as required (Article 7.25.2, page 120). The employer retains the right to limit the number of leaves granted and may replace members on sabbatical leave when necessary (Article 12.04, page 35).

Compensation for sabbatical leaves is also addressed in Article 22.09, which states that compensation will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association.

Source:
Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2018-2021

For Pregnancy Leave, as outlined in section 14.04 of the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (pages 36-37), the following conditions apply for entitlement:

1. The Employer supplements Employment Insurance maternity benefits up to 100% of the employee's nominal earnings during Pregnancy Leave, and up to seventeen weeks of leave is granted in accordance with Ontario's Employment Standards Act.

2. To qualify for supplementary unemployment benefits, a member must have completed at least twelve months of continuous full-time active service with the University immediately preceding the Pregnancy Leave.

3. The member must give at least two weeks' written notice to the Employer of the intent to take Pregnancy Leave and the date they intend to commence it.

4. The member must apply for and be in receipt of Employment Insurance maternity benefits, providing the employer with official documentation regarding EI benefits.

5. During Pregnancy Leave, the member continues to accumulate vacation credits and seniority, while Group Benefits and Pension contributions (based on 100% salary) continue during this period.

6. Any period of absence immediately preceding or following such Pregnancy Leave shall be considered a leave of absence without pay, except that the University will continue to pay its share of Group Benefits premiums during a Parental Leave if the employee agrees in writing to pay their share.

7. Immediately following the completion of a Pregnancy Leave and any related leave of absence without pay, the employee is required to return to work for a period equal to the length of the Pregnancy Leave taken (normally 17 weeks). Failure to do so will result in a requirement to repay the Supplemental Unemployment Benefits to the University.

answer:
According to Article 5.75 of the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 100/243), the collective agreement provides as follows regarding discipline:

* Discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases. (5.75.2)
* Just cause is defined as:
	+ Gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behaviour and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another Member; Members of the University community and/or students of the University community.
	+ Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility as defined in this Collective Agreement either through incompetence or neglect of duty to students or scholarly professional pursuits. (5.75.2(a) and (b))
* Just cause must be interpreted in the context of a University environment including the principles of tenure where applicable. (5.75.3)
* Discipline shall be imposed only in compliance with principles of natural justice and due process. Accordingly, the Member has a fundamental right to know, in a timely manner, the nature of the allegations against him/her, and the right to respond to such allegations. (5.75.4 and 5.75.5)
* The following are the only forms of discipline which may be taken by the Employer against Members:
	+ A full-time Member: letter of reprimand, suspension with pay or without pay, withholding of an annual increment, or dismissal.
	+ A sessional or part-time Member: letter of reprimand, suspension with pay or without pay, removal of seniority and/or Establishment, or dismissal. (5.75.5)

Additionally, the collective agreement provides that:

* The Employer shall commence an investigation within twenty (20) working days when a matter is brought to their attention that may lead to the imposition of discipline under this Article. (5.75.6)
* The Member and the Union shall be notified in writing of the nature of the allegation(s) upon commencement of the investigation, except in circumstances where to do so would compromise the integrity of the investigation. (5.75.6)

It's worth noting that non-compliance with this article will not result in discipline being automatically void. The effect of any prejudice to a Member as a result of non-compliance may be considered by an Arbitrator. (Collective Agreement 2011-14, page 100/243)

The Faculty Affairs Committee (FAC) is addressed in the Laurentian University Collective Agreement under Article 8. The purpose of the FAC, as stated in Article 8.01, is to provide the President with reasoned recommendations on applications from members regarding renewal of probationary appointments, promotion, tenure, research or travel fund allocation (when available), sabbatical leave, and other matters that may be referred to the Committee.

The FAC's membership is composed of one tenured member elected by each University Department, two members at large elected from the ranks of tenure or tenure-tracked members, a full-time member-at-large elected to serve as an alternate, the Dean of Arts at Laurentian University (non-voting), the University Registrar or a senior academic administrator (non-voting, who shall be the Chair and Committee Secretary), and all bargaining unit members serving a two-year term (Source: Article 8.02).

Applications must be filed by September 30 of each year, including all necessary supporting documentation. Members on probationary appointments shall normally begin to undergo a formal tenure evaluation by the FAC in their final year of probationary status. A member may apply for tenure evaluation one year prior to the final year of his/her probation.

The FAC's procedures are outlined in Article 8.06, which includes provisions on quorum, confidentiality, meeting schedule, voting and minutes, and requests by the Union or University to meet with the committee before its first meeting in September (Source: Article 8.06). According to Article 23 and Article 24 of the Collective Agreement 2018-2021, the following are the conditions that apply to the grievance procedure:

**Mandatory Time Limits**: The time limits set out in Articles 23 and 24 are mandatory (Article 23.09, page not specified; Article 24.06, page 52). Failure to comply strictly with these time limits, except by written agreement of the parties, shall result in the grievance being deemed to have been abandoned.

**Written Notice**: Written notice of referral to arbitration must be given to the other party within the time limits set out in Article 23.05 (Article 24.01, page 52).

**Appointment of Nominees**: Each party must appoint its nominee to the Arbitration Board within 21 Working days of receipt of written notice (Article 24.01, page 52).

**Chairperson Selection**: The nominees shall attempt to select a chairperson by agreement. If they are unable to agree, the Minister of Labour for the Province of Ontario may effect such appointment upon application by either party (Article 24.01, page 52).

**Conflict of Interest**: No person may be appointed as an arbitrator who has been involved in attempting to negotiate or settle the grievance (Article 24.02, page 52).

These conditions aim to ensure a fair and efficient process for resolving grievances through arbitration.

Please note that Article 6.40 outlines a specific procedure for handling grievances related to patents and copyright disputes, which is separate from the general grievance procedure outlined in Articles 23 and 24.

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement defines the arbitration procedure through Schedule "S" - Expedited Med-Arbitration Processes (pages unspecified). Here are the key points:

1. Parties may be represented by legal counsel for expedited med-arbitration dates.
2. The parties will agree to up to four (4) dates for expedited med-arbitration for each year of the term of the Collective Agreement.
3. At least 60 days prior to each expedited med-arbitration date, the parties will agree on the grievances to be dealt with on that day.
4. Up to three (3) grievances will be heard on each expedited med-arbitration date.
5. Forty-five (45) days prior to each expedited med-arbitration date, a party may make requests for production of documents from the other party. Disclosure will be provided within fifteen (15) days.
6. Each grievance proceeding to expedited med-arbitration will be heard and determined on the basis of written briefs prepared by the parties as supplemented by brief oral arguments.
7. The parties will exchange written briefs at least fourteen (14) days in advance of the expedited med-arbitration.
8. The parties' written briefs for each expedited med-arbitration will contain a summary of the facts the party will rely on, a copy of all documents that the party will rely on in support of its case, as well a written argument in summary form and a copy of all cases on which the party relies. The briefs will be sent to the med-arbitrator seven (7) days in advance of the med-arbitration date.
9. In the event that a party does not deliver its written brief within the time required under paragraph 7 above, or with the content required under paragraph 7 above, the other party may, at its sole discretion, cancel the med-arbitration date.
10. Any procedural disputes shall be resolved by the arbitrator assigned to the med-arbitration date in question on an expedited basis.
11. Awards arising out of this process are non-precedential and may not be referred to or relied upon by the Parties in any other proceedings unless mutually agreed otherwise. Negotiated settlements may or may not be precedential as agreed by the parties.
12. The med-arbitration will be heard by William Kaplan, Sheri Price, Elizabeth McIntyre, and Brian Sheehan on a rotational basis.

The leave must be in the best interests of the University, and the maximum length of leaves to be granted during a Member's academic career shall normally not exceed two (2) years.

If the Vice-President, Academic and Provost finds it necessary to refuse Members their study leave on financial grounds after the leave had been approved, that Member shall be given priority within the Member's Department/School for a study leave for the following year (page 131).

answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement defines and describes the following with regards to appointments, promotions, and tenure for full-time faculty members:

1. Appointment: Initial appointments can be at one of four ranks - Full Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, or Lecturer (11.02). The categories of appointment are Tenured, Probationary (tenure-track), and Limited Term (11.03).

2. Promotion:
   - For Assistant Professor, a candidate must hold a Doctorate or a Master’s degree plus satisfactory performance and demonstrated scholarly activity over five years (11.04c).
   - For Associate Professor, a candidate must have a Doctorate or equivalent degree, demonstrate good quality teaching, good quality scholarly activity including at least one peer-reviewed work, and have a minimum of five years’ satisfactory performance as an Assistant Professor (11.04d).
   - For Full Professor, a candidate must have successfully met all requirements for Associate Professor, shown evidence of scholarly activity throughout their career, been judged by at least three referees, and accumulated ten years of satisfactory full-time teaching experience (11.04d).

3. Tenure: Tenure means permanency of appointment, it protects free criticism and independent judgment as part of academic freedom (13.06c). It can be terminated through resignation, retirement, dismissal for cause, or as otherwise stated in the agreement (13.06c).

References:
- LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2018-2021, pages 24-25 and 21 for ranks, promotions, and tenure; page 14 for categories.

According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, the rights, responsibilities, and duties of members are defined as follows:

1. Rights: Members have the right to engage in teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, scholarly activity, university governance and administrative duties, outside professional activities, service to the community, and other paid activity (Article 2.00).

2. Responsibilities (for Members of the Regular Stream): Members are expected to participate actively in teaching, scholarly activity, and university governance and administrative duties, although not necessarily in all three in any one given year. Their responsibilities related to teaching consist of those duties which are assigned by the Dean/Director of the Library as per Article 2.10 - Academic Workload (Article 2.00). Certain specific duties related to teaching may also be assigned on an ad hoc basis to ensure a good and proper functioning of the University. A Member's responsibilities relating to scholarly activity and university governance are inherent in their status as academics. Members have an obligation to develop and maintain their scholarly competence and effectiveness as teachers within their area of expertise, inform students regarding their methods of evaluation and instructional methods, and be available for reasonable consultation with students (Article 2.00, Priority I, A).

3. Responsibilities (for Members of the Alternate Stream): Similar to Members of the Regular Stream, but they have responsibilities relating only to teaching and university governance, not scholarly activity (Article 2.00).

4. Duties: Certain specific duties related to teaching, scholarly activity, and university governance may also be assigned by the Dean/University Librarian on an ad hoc basis in order to ensure a good and proper functioning of the University (Article 2.00). Members are expected to teach the assigned courses to students registered in them at the time and place designated by the Dean, and have an obligation to be available to students for consultation during a regular teaching term for at least one hour per week for a three-credit course (Article 5.15.6).

In addition, the agreement recognizes Indigenous knowledge as a vital part of knowledge transmission within the context of Indigenous Peoples living in place, and sets out specific features of academic responsibilities related to teaching, including an obligation for Members to develop and maintain their scholarly competence and effectiveness as teachers (Article 5.15.5). The agreement also acknowledges that the Employer has retained management rights, which include the right to discipline for just cause, and that these rights shall be exercised in a manner consistent with the provisions of the Agreement (Article 6.01).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement provides that disciplinary action shall be just and reasonable, commensurate with the offense, and follow a principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases. Cause for disciplinary measures includes serious unprofessional behavior and failure to comply with the provisions of the agreement (excluding minor technical violations).

The formal disciplinary measures that may be taken against a Member include:
- A letter of reprimand specifying the grounds and adding it to the personnel file.
- Withholding an annual increment.
- Suspension without pay, with the reduction in pay computed as one two hundred and sixtieth (1/260) of normal salary per day of suspension.
- Suspension with pay, only if the Vice-President, Academic cites the suspension with pay as a disciplinary measure.
- Dismissal for just cause, as per Article 5.80 – Dismissal Procedures.

For sessional or part-time Members, the other forms of discipline include a letter of reprimand, suspension with pay, suspension without pay, removal of seniority and/or Establishment, and dismissal for Part-time Clinicians.
