1. Full-time academic staff, including librarians, are required to submit an annual report by June 1 of each year, reviewing their Academic Activity for the period May 1-April 31 (LUFA-H, 17). In the case of Sabbatical/Study Leave, this report should generally be submitted within one month upon return from leave. The annual report should consist of:
   - An updated curriculum vitae using the HU template
   - Copies of Senate-approved standardized student evaluations
   - A completed report based on the HU report template
   - Electronic copies of presentations
   - An update on doctoral studies (LUFA-H, 17)

2. Sessional Members are required to submit brief annual reports in electronic format to the Dean/University Librarian (LUFA-H, not specified page number). These reports should include a current curriculum vitae as well as a current teaching dossier as defined in Article 5.50 – Assessment of a Member’s Performance. At their discretion, Sessional Members may also include material related to their scholarly or creativity activity, professional development, university governance, outside professional activities, and service to the community (LUFA-H, not specified page number).

3. Full-time members of the Bargaining Unit shall submit a written Report on their activities for the preceding twelve months, from 1 May to 30 April, to the President by June 22nd. The report will cover all components of members’ activities as described in Article 10, Academic Activity. In preparing their Annual Report, members shall use the standardized form approved by the University of Sudbury Senate and provided by the Registrar, and it is also their responsibility to provide annually an up-to-date C.V. with their Annual Report (LUFA-H, not specified page number).

Faculty appointments at Laurentian University, according to the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020 (page 23), are made through a process that prioritizes Members with established courses. If an appointment cannot be filled by a Member with establishment, appointments will be made from rosters of potential instructors who have taught in the department in the previous academic year. If a suitable candidate cannot be found in the roster, the appointments will be advertised on employment websites (page 23).

The application process includes the submission of a curriculum vitae, a current teaching dossier, reference letters, and any relevant supplementary information (page 23). Three academic letters of reference speaking specifically to the position will be sent directly to the Employer for new applicants, new course offerings, or courses out of the applicant's expertise or department (page 23).

For adjunct faculty appointments, a list is tabled at Senate each month, including the names, Department/School affiliations, periods of appointment, a justification for each appointment, highest degree held, year obtained, current institution and rank (position), at that institution. Adjunct faculty Members may become Sessional Members if they carry duties consistent with the Collective Agreement, and they will be included in the faculty listing on Department/School websites (pages 7-8).

Cross appointments, which allow Members to be appointed to more than one Department/School of the University, can be made for academic teaching/scholarly or professional reasons, but only with the consent of all Departments/Schools concerned. Cross appointments are made by the Employer for a fixed period not exceeding five years and may be renewed or altered with the consent of the Member and on the recommendations of the Department(s)/School(s) concerned (pages 7-8).

Assessments for the renewal, promotion, and tenure of Members are based on an assessment of their performance in teaching, scholarly activity, and university, professional, and community service, as set out in Articles 10 and 11.04 of the Collective Agreement (page 11). The nature and scope of past teaching activities are taken into account in assessing a Member, and the assessors will look for evidence that the applicant has recognized problems in teaching, taken steps to improve, and made improvements that are reflected in independent evidence provided by the member (page 11). The assessors shall be flexible in assessing stronger performance in some areas against weaker performance in other areas, but they shall not recommend tenure for an applicant if teaching performance is judged unsatisfactory or if the applicant is not engaged in a program of scholarly activity (page 11).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines the maximum norms for assigned workloads for both Teaching Members and Professional Librarian and Archivist Members.

For Teaching Members, the maximum normal teaching load per academic year is two and one-half (2 ½) full courses or fifteen (15) credit equivalents in all Faculties. In the Faculty of Science and Engineering, the maximum normal teaching load is two (2) full courses or twelve (12) credit equivalents. Members on a twelve (12) month limited-term appointment may have a teaching load of three (3) credits above the normal teaching load, but only for a maximum of twelve (12) months.

For Professional Librarian and Archivist Members, the normal hours of scheduled student contact shall not exceed twelve (12) per week.

The composition of the workload may vary with the capabilities of the Members and the need to maximize their potential, taking into account any obligations placed on them within the University's operations. The workload can also include faculty outreach and liaison, participation in research, support for scholarly communication, evaluation, measurement, and analysis of user needs and library services, research services, extension, and other activities related to programs at the University, and any other relevant activities (source: Collective Agreement 2008-11, page 70).

In addition, the annual academic workload shall be determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible, taking into account various factors such as the needs of the member’s program, the number of hours of preparation, grading and administration per course, the level of each course, the amount of academic supervision of undergraduate and graduate students, and the method of delivery of each course (source: Collective Agreement 2018-2021, pages 20-21).

(a) As the fundamental objective of the University is the search for new knowledge and the free dissemination of what is

answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides that academic freedom is essential for the teaching and research activities of the University (0.02 Academic freedom). Academic freedom includes the right to investigate, speculate, and comment publicly, to carry out research, to publish results, to choose and pursue teaching methods and content, to state professional views, to discuss and criticize, including respectful criticism of the Employer, the Union, and any public or private institution, and to be free from institutional censorship (3.10.2). Academic freedom does not require neutrality in expression or attitude and does not confer legal immunity (3.10.2). The principle and practice of collegial governance are essential for the exercise of academic freedom within the University (3.10.3). Members have the right to exercise their civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded, or hindered by the Employer (3.10.4). The Employer shall not abridge academic freedom on any grounds, including claims of institutional autonomy (3.10.5). Members have the right to privacy, consistent with the traditions of academic freedom (3.10.6, 3.15.1).

The Collective Agreement between the Laurentian University Faculty Association and the Employer outlines several rules concerning research and development.

1. Inventions, improvements, or discoveries made by the Members (faculty) are assigned to the University, with both parties sharing equally in the "net proceeds" derived from them (6.30.8, Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 6).

2. The University shall not use its name in connection with inventions in which it has no interest, without mutual agreement (6.30.9, page 1).

3. 4. The Employer shall not enter into agreements to create a consortia of universities or government departments or private companies for the purposes of research or development or commercial exploitation without securing the same rights, privileges, and benefits for Members who may be seconded to or employed by such consortia, departments, or private companies (6.30.11, page 1).

For scholarly activity, Members have the right and responsibility to devote a reasonable proportion of their time to research and academic activities that contribute to the enhancement, creation, and dissemination of knowledge (5.15.20, page 6). answer:
Academic freedom, as defined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 2), includes several conditions:

1. The right to search for truth, knowledge, and understanding, and to express freely what one believes (3.10.2).
2. Freedom in teaching, research, and scholarship, including the right to disseminate and publish results (3.10.2).
3. Freedom to produce and perform creative works (3.10.2).
4. Freedom to acquire, preserve, and provide access to documentary material in all formats (3.10.2).
5. Freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies (3.10.2).
6. Freedom to engage in service to the institution and the community (3.10.2).
7. Freedom to express one’s opinion about the University, its administration, and the system in which one works (3.10.2).
8. Academic freedom does not confer legal immunity but requires the acknowledgement of the work of others and the acceptance of responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances (3.10.2).
9. The principle and practice of collegial governance are essential for the exercise of academic freedom within the University (3.10.3).
10. Academic freedom also entails the right of academic staff to exercise their civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded, or hindered by the Employer (3.10.4).
11. The Employer shall not abridge academic freedom on any grounds, including claims of institutional autonomy (3.10.5).
12. Members have a right to privacy, consistent with the traditions of Academic Freedom and the provisions of this Article (3.15.1).

In addition, the Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (page 3) further explains that academic freedom makes commitment possible, does not require neutrality in expression or attitude, and carries the responsibility to respect the right of other members of the academic community to express their opinions (0.02 Academic freedom, section b). The rules concerning the redundancy committee, as outlined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement, are as follows:

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines the rights, responsibilities, and duties of the members of the bargaining unit. According to Article 11 of the Collective Agreement 2008-2011, there are several rules concerning redundancy:

answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement addresses health, safety, and security through Article 3.25 - Health, Safety, and Security. According to the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 22), the Employer recognizes a responsibility to provide an environment intended to protect the health, safety, and security of employees as they carry out their responsibilities. To achieve this, the Parties are bound by the Occupational Health and Safety Act R.S.O 1990 as revised and in effect July 1, 2008. The Employer agrees to maintain a Joint Health and Safety Committee that will independently consider matters concerning the health and safety of employees and students.

Members who have reason to believe that a work situation is likely to endanger them have the right to refuse unsafe work pursuant to and in accordance with the provisions of the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act (Article 3.25.3).

Moreover, the Union shall observe and assist in the implementation of rules adopted to protect the health and safety of employees and to maintain the security of persons and premises (Article 3.25.2).

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement defines and describes tuition fee exemption as follows:

1. Full-time Members and retired full-time Members are eligible for tuition fee exemption (Article 8.50.1).
2. Spouses and dependants (children up to the age of 26, including natural, step, adopted children, wards, and other children for whom the Member is the primary caregiver) of all full-time Members, retired full-time Members, spouses and dependants of Members who died while in full-time employment of the University are also eligible for tuition fee exemption (Article 8.50.1).

4. International tuition fees will only be covered up to the rate of domestic tuition fees, and the remaining balance is the responsibility of the student (Article 8.50.2).
5. The employer reserves the right to modify or rescind this policy depending on the development of future government policy that has a bearing on this matter (Article 8.50.4).

answer: The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides that discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.1). Just cause for disciplinary measures includes serious unprofessional behavior and failure to comply with any provisions of the collective agreement, minor technical violations excepted (5.75.2). The forms of discipline that may be taken against a full-time member include a letter of reprimand, suspension with pay, suspension without pay, withholding of an annual increment, and dismissal (5.75.3). For a sessional or part-time member, the forms of discipline include a letter of reprimand, suspension with pay, suspension without pay, removal of seniority and/or establishment, and dismissal (5.75.5). Discipline shall be imposed only in compliance with principles of natural justice and due process, and the member has a fundamental right to know the nature of the allegations against them and to respond to such allegations (5.75.4). The collective agreement also specifies that cases involving the inability of a member to perform reasonable duties due to physical or mental illness shall be treated separately from cases for disciplinary measures (5.75.6). Removal from office, in the context of the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, is referred to as "Dismissal" (Article 4.65 - Dismissal Procedures). According to the agreement, dismissal means the termination for just cause of a term appointment or a probationary appointment before the end of the stated contractual period, or the termination of a tenure appointment for cause at any time other than normal retirement (4.65.1). Just cause for dismissal is defined as gross misconduct or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibilities as defined in the agreement either through incompetence or neglect of duties (4.65.2).

However, cases involving the inability of a member to perform reasonable duties by reason of physical or emotional illness shall be treated separately from cases of dismissal for cause (4.65.3). If such inability has been established, leave shall be granted, and the case dealt with within the University sickness and disability provisions (4.65.3a). The agreement defines promotions for members of the teaching faculty in the Laurentian University Faculty Association as follows:

1. For the rank of Lecturer, there are two qualifications: a Master's degree or equivalent degree, or a Baccalaureate degree and an appropriate professional designation (Article 5.10.2 (a) i, ii).

2. For the rank of Assistant Professor, there are three qualifications: a Doctoral degree, a Master's degree or equivalent, and satisfactory performance of the member's responsibilities and duties over a five-year period, with demonstrated evidence of scholarly activity as per Article 5.15; or, in the Department of Law and Justice, eight years of full-time university education during which time the member must have obtained a LL.B. and an appropriate Master’s degree (Article 5.10.2 (b) i, ii, iii).

3. For the rank of Associate Professor, there are four qualifications: a Doctoral degree, satisfactory teaching quality as determined solely by the method of teaching evaluation mandated by the Collective Agreement, evidence of scholarly activity that is of good quality, and at least five years of full-time teaching and/or research in a university or an institution of equivalent level or at least five years of professional experience judged to be relevant for teaching at the university level. In exceptional cases, the requirement for scholarly activity may be replaced by a consistently demonstrated quality of teaching and tutorial activity that clearly indicates outstanding qualities as a teacher (Article 5.10.2 (c) i, ii, iii, iv, v).

4. For the rank of Full Professor, there are two qualifications: a Doctoral degree, and teaching quality that is satisfactory as determined solely by the method of teaching evaluation mandated by the Collective Agreement, and shown evidence of scholarly activity throughout the member’s career and after her/his promotion to Associate Professor that ranks as a recognized contribution to the scholarly field or professional activity concerned (Article 5.10.2 (d) i, ii, iii).

According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement, discipline is only for cause (5.75.1). Discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.1). Just cause is defined as gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another member, members of the University community, and/or students of the University community, or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility as defined in this Collective Agreement either through incompetence or neglect of duty to students or scholarly professional pursuits (5.75.2). Discipline must be imposed in compliance with principles of natural justice and due process (5.75.4). The member has a fundamental right to know, in a timely manner, the nature of the allegations against him/her, and the right to respond to such allegations (5.75.4). The only forms of discipline that may be taken against a full-time member include a letter of reprimand, suspension with or without pay, withholding of an annual increment, or dismissal (5.75.5). The only forms of discipline that may be taken against a sessional or part-time member include a letter of reprimand, suspension with or without pay, removal of seniority and/or establishment, or dismissal (5.75.5). When the Employer becomes aware of a matter that may lead to the imposition of discipline, including investigations triggered by a formal complaint pursuant to a discrimination and harassment policy, the Employer shall commence an investigation within twenty working days (5.75.6). The member and the Union shall be notified in writing of the nature of the allegation(s) upon commencement of the investigation (5.75.6).

- In the event of a cancellation, the Employer shall attempt to find work of equivalent value for which the Sessional Member is qualified, and failing this, shall pay a cancellation fee of fifteen percent (15%) of the agreed salary as outlined in the Letter of Appointment.

According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement, Full-time academic staff have the right and responsibility to devote a reasonable proportion of their time to scholarly activity. This activity includes (but is not limited to) research directed towards a contribution to knowledge, the dissemination of its results, participation in academic activities that contribute to the enhancement, creation, and dissemination of knowledge, and creative and professional activities which contribute to one's discipline (11.03, 5.15.20-22).

Members are also encouraged to deposit one signed copy of their published material in the Huntington University Library and a hard or electronic copy in the Office of the President (11.03, 5.15.25). They have the right to participate in the activities of professional or learned societies, providing such activities do not conflict with the reasonable fulfillment of assigned duties (11.03, 5.15.26).

For the purposes of the Collective Agreement, scholarly activity does not normally include research directly related to the immediate and normal preparation for teaching activity (5.15.23). The Parties also agree that Members shall indicate affiliation with the University and acknowledge their indebtedness to students and their academic colleagues in relation to their own research (5.15.24).

D'après l'article 12 de la Convention Collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne (Source : Document non spécifié, page 34), voici les principales dispositions relatives aux congés sabbatiques :

answer:
Les activités universitaires sont définies à l'article 10 de la Convention collective 2015-2018. Les membres de l'unité de négociation s'engagent à effectuer les tâches d'enseignement, de recherche, à fournir leurs services à l'Université et à la profession et à la communauté. Les conditions applicables à ces activités universitaires sont que :

- Les activités doivent être effectuées dans des proportions raisonnables, variant selon les personnes.
- Les membres ont jusqu'au 31 août pour répondre par écrit aux réserves du Recteur concernant leur rendement en matière d'activités universitaires.
- Si la réponse écrite du membre ne répond pas de manière satisfaisante aux réserves du Recteur, le cas est confié au Comité des affaires professorales. Les motifs à l'appui sont fournis par écrit.
- Le Comité des affaires professorales évalue les activités du membre, les réserves écrites du Recteur et, le cas échéant, la réponse du membre. Le comité fait au Recteur une recommandation sur la question de savoir si les activités sont satisfaisantes ou non, en précisant par écrit les raisons de sa recommandation et, le cas échéant, la réponse du membre.
- La recommandation du comité est faite au plus tard 28 jours civils après que le cas lui a été soumis par le Recteur.
- Le Recteur évalue et prend en compte la recommandation du Comité des affaires professorales et rend sa décision finale en se reportant aux points pertinents de l'article 10. Lorsqu'il s'agit d'accepter une recommandation positive, l'augmentation est accordée rétroactivement au 1er juillet.

Ces règles sont décrites dans la Convention collective 2015-2018, pages 79 et 32.

answer:
Selon l'article 6.35 et l'article 15 de la Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne, voici les informations clés sur les droits d'auteur :

**Droits d'auteur revenant aux Membres :**

* Le membre conserve les droits d'auteur pour toute création intellectuelle sauf stipulation contraire (art. 6.35.1).
* Les créations couvertes par cette disposition comprennent notamment des œuvres imprimées, des programmes informatiques, du matériel pédagogique en ligne, des tableaux, des sculptures, des films, des diapositives et d'autres (art. 6.35.1).

**Droits d'auteur revenant à l'Université :**

* Les parties conviennent que l'Université détient les droits d'auteur pour toute création intellectuelle produite par un membre dans le cadre de ses fonctions à l'Université (art. 6.35.2).
* L'Université conserve également les droits d'auteur pour toutes les œuvres originales, y compris des livres, textes, articles, monographies, glossaires, bibliographies, matériel cartographique, affiches, manuels d'étude, plans de cours, examens, directives de travaux et autres supports visuels (art. 15.01).

**Copie du membre :**

* Si possible après en avoir fait la demande, le membre doit recevoir une copie de toute propriété intellectuelle qu'il a produite pour l'Université, sans que le coût excède celui du moyen utilisé (art. 6.35.16).
* Cela signifie que les membres ont droit à une copie des œuvres pour lesquelles l'Université détient les droits d'auteur, moyennant un coût limité.

**Effacement ou destruction de l'œuvre :**

* En cas de désir de l'Université d'effacer ou de détruire en tout ou en partie un ouvrage pour lequel elle détient les droits d'auteur, le membre doit être notifié et a droit à une copie de l'œuvre (art. 6.35.17).

La Convention collective garantit ainsi que les membres conservent les droits d'auteur sur leurs créations sauf stipulation contraire, tandis que l'Université détient les droits d'auteur pour toutes les œuvres produites par les membres dans le cadre de leurs fonctions.

Pourtant, lorsque le salaire du membre dépasse 164 136 $ par an, il n’y a pas de telle augmentation (source : page 78).

En outre, les augmentations au mérite et pour les promotions sont accordées selon l'article 8.15 ainsi que l'article 8.25 – Augmentation au mérite (source : page 78).

En outre, la rémunération des membres chargés de cours qui enseignent un cours "didactique" à l’École des sciences de l’éducation ou un cours "teachable" à "The School of Education" est fixée proportionnellement à six cent dollars (600 $) par étudiant jusqu’à concurrence de la rémunération maximale pour un Chargé de cours avec statut prioritaire pour ce type de cours (source : page 4).

Enfin, dans le cadre d'un congé d'études, un membre reçoit toutes les augmentations générales consenties aux membres du même rang, après avoir reçu une évaluation positive de son rendement, selon l'article 20.34 de la Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne de 2015-2018 (source : page 34).

Selon la Convention collective 2015-2018 (page 45), un grief est une allégation, un litige ou une plainte concernant l’interprétation, l’application, l’administration ou la violation présumée de la présente Convention collective. Selon l'article 8 de la Convention Collective 2018-2021, un Comité des affaires professorales est créé pour faire des recommandations justifiées au Recteur à la suite des demandes faites par les membres en matière de renouvellement de nominations à l'essai, promotion, permanence, subventions de recherche ou de voyages et congés sabbatiques (page 10).

Le Comité est composé de :

* Un représentant ayant la permanence élu par le Département parmi les membres permanents (article 8.02.a, page 10)
* Deux Membres non désignés, ayant la permanence ou à l’essai élus (article 8.02.b, page 10)
* Un membre non désigné à plein temps pour agir comme substitut (article 8.02.c, page 10)
* Le Doyen de la Faculté des arts de l'Université Laurentienne, sans droit de vote (article 8.02.d, page 10)

En outre, si le Recteur a des réserves à propos du rendement d'un membre concernant les activités universitaires décrites à l'article 10, il envoie un exposé de ses réserves au membre au plus tard le 31 juillet (article 20.04.a, page 41). Le membre a jusqu'au 31 août pour y répondre par écrit (article 20.04.b, page 41). Si la réponse écrite du membre ne répond pas de manière satisfaisante aux réserves du Recteur, le cas est confié au Comité des affaires professorales et les motifs à l'appui sont communiqués au membre (article 20.04.c, page 41).

Source : Convention collective 2018-2021, pages 10, 41 et 59.

La Convention collective 2008-11 et la Convention collective 2011-14 établissent les règles concernant les congés de maternité pour les membres à temps plein et les membres chargés de cours permanents qui sont enceintes.

Selon la Convention collective 2008-11 (p. 148), une membre a droit à un congé de maternité de dix-sept (17) semaines, pendant lesquelles elle reçoit de l’Employeur un montant équivalent à la différence entre les prestations de l’Assurance Emploi (AE) reçues par le membre et cent pour cent (100 %) de son traitement normal. Si le membre est inadmissible ou exclu des prestations de l’AE, l’Employeur maintient le membre à cent pour cent (100 %) de son traitement normal pendant la période de congé.

La Convention collective 2011-14 (p. 141) contient des règles similaires pour les congés de maternité.

La Convention collective 2017-2020 établit également des règles concernant les congés parentaux (p. 76). Les membres ne sont pas tenus d’enseigner pendant le semestre en cours après leur retour du congé parental.

Les propriétés intellectuelles produites par le membre pour l'Université, pour lesquelles celle-ci détient les droits d'auteur, doivent être remises au membre si possible après demande, et le coût de cette copie ne doit pas dépasser le prix du ruban, film, enregistrement ou autre moyen utilisé (Article 6.35.16). De plus, la Convention stipule que si l'Université désire effacer ou détruire un ouvrage pour lequel elle détient les droits d'auteur, elle doit en informer le membre (Article 6.35.17).

Lorsque des demandes de subventions de source interne ou externe requièrent une présélection ou une évaluation, l’Employeur affiche la composition du comité de sélection sur le site Web du Bureau de la RDC, et la participation des Membres du corps professoral au comité de sélection est encouragée (article 6.15.2).

Les règles concernant les dossiers personnels des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne, selon la Convention collective 2015-2018 (page 42), sont les suivantes :

La convention stipule également que l'Université a le devoir essentiel d'assurer la priorité des objectifs pédagogiques, notamment en matière de qualité de l'enseignement, de recherche et des services de bibliothèque, ainsi que la protection de la liberté universitaire ou académique (source : 10.15.1).

La convention collective traite de la question des surcharges de travail en article 8.35, qui se divise en deux sous-articles.

**ARTICLE 8.35.1**

Selon l'article 8.35.1 (page non précisée, mais dans le texte fourni), tous les professeurs à temps plein, peu importe le rang, qui donnent un cours en surcharge et rémunéré, reçoivent une allocation indiquée pour les cours commençant après les dates précisées.

On remarque que cette disposition est apparue trois fois dans l'extrait fourni. Le montant des allocations varie selon la date de début du cours :

- Pour les cours commençant après le 1er juillet 2017, les sommes sont de 10 322 $ pour un cours entier et de 5 161 $ pour un demi-cours.
- Pour ceux commençant après le 1er juillet 2018, il s'agit de 10 487 $ pour un cours entier et de 5 244 $ pour un demi-cours.
- Enfin, pour les cours commençant après le 1er juillet 2019, ces montants sont respectivement de 10 665 $ et 5 333 $.

**ARTICLE 8.35.2**

L'article 8.35.2 mentionne une situation où un cours d'éducation permanente risque d'être annulé. Dans ce cas, un membre peut accepter de donner le cours (page non précisée).

Il convient de noter que l'article 8.35.1 est apparu trois fois avec des dates différentes et qu'il y a eu un changement dans les montants alloués pour les surcharges entre 2008, 2017 et 2019.

Pour répondre à la question :

La convention collective traite de la question des surcharges de travail en indiquant que les professeurs à temps plein qui donnent un cours en surcharge et rémunéré reçoivent une allocation spécifique selon les dates de début du cours.

Selon la convention, la recommandation enseignants passe par un processus collégial d'évaluation par les pairs (Article 11.01). L'apport et les recommandations des membres travaillant dans la même discipline que celle où une nomination est prévue sont reconnus d'importance (Article 11.01). Toutefois, l'employeur détermine le nombre de postes à combler au sein du corps professoral pour permettre à l'Université de remplir ses objectifs et sa mission, et toute décision finale relève du Conseil des régents et du Recteur (Article 11.01).

1. Expérience (Clause 5.10.2 (c) (iv))

3. Travaux d'érudition (Clause 5.10.2 (c) (iii))
4. Participation à la régie et à l'administration de l'Université (Clause 5.15.26)
5. Contributions exceptionnelles dans un domaine pour contrebalancer un rendement moindre dans un autre domaine (Clause 5.50.4)

La recommandation enseignants est faite après une évaluation qui inclut les opinions de la majorité et de la minorité, le cas échéant (ANNEXE N, Convention collective 2011-14).

answer:
La Convention collective prévoit que le processus de grief se déroule en deux étapes :

1. Étape 1 - Procédure informelle de grief : le Syndicat et l'Employeur conviennent de faire tous les efforts raisonnables pour régler informellement les griefs de façon expéditive et à l'amiable. Il est convenu qu'aucun grief ne peut être déposé avant que l'administrateur concerné ait eu l'occasion de corriger la situation dont se plaint le Syndicat. Cette plainte est discutée avec le membre de l'administration dans les 30 jours ouvrables suivant le moment où les circonstances donnant lieu à la plainte sont venues ou auraient dû raisonnablement venir à l'attention du Syndicat. L'administrateur donnera une réponse écrite dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la discussion. Si la plainte n’est pas réglée, elle sera acheminée au Recteur dans une 2° étape dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réponse.

2. Étape 2 - Procédure de grief par écrit : dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réponse mentionnée à la 1ère étape de la procédure, le Syndicat soumet par écrit au Recteur de l'Université un grief, en précisant la nature du grief, les dispositions particulières de la Convention collective qui sont présumées violées et la solution recherchée. Dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant le dépôt du grief, une réunion des représentants de l'Employeur avec le Syndicat et les membres concernés a lieu, à sa ou leur demande. Les Parties font des efforts raisonnables pour régler le grief et la réponse de l'Employeur est donnée dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réunion (source document : Convention collective 2017-2020, pages 25-26).
